paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take home, friend. This writer never pretends he's fine. He's crying, he's being taunted, and he even asks God, "Why have You forgotten me?" (Psalm 42:9). And God lets that question stay in the Bible. So you can bring Him the hard stuff too, because He can handle it.

Now look at what the writer does with all that ache. He talks to his own soul: "Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him…" (Psalm 42:5). It's not a one-time pep talk, either. That line comes back in Psalm 42:11 and again in Psalm 43:5. I spent years in a dark drawer, and I'm telling you, hope sometimes has to be said out loud, more than once, and then said AGAIN!

And watch where he points that hope. He asks for God's light and truth to lead him to the altar of God, "to God, my greatest joy" (Psalm 43:3-4). He doesn't say, "Fix everything first." He says, "Lead me to YOU." So when your soul is thirsty and the waves are rolling, baker, put your hope in God. He's your Savior and your God, and the praise is still coming.
